title: Accessibility at a sharply larger regular cardinal
statement: Use the universes, smallness, compactness and accessibility conventions of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and quasicategories, coherent diagrams and colimits from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\lambda<\kappa$ be infinite regular cardinals in the smaller universe such that $\mu^\nu<\kappa$ for every cardinal $\mu<\kappa$ and every cardinal $\nu<\lambda$. Let $\mathcal C$ be a $\lambda$-accessible infinity category. Then $\mathcal C$ is $\kappa$-accessible.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9, printed p. 426 (PDF p. 444), with the cardinal relation spelled out as immediately before Lemma 5.4.2.8 and in Definition A.2.6.3. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: By [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], choose an essentially small full subcategory $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal C$ of $\lambda$-compact objects generating $\mathcal C$ under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits. The category $\mathcal C$ is locally small. Every $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory is $\lambda$-filtered: any $\lambda$-small test simplicial set is also $\kappa$-small, so its cocone exists. Thus $\mathcal C$ admits all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Restricting the defining preservation property to this subclass also shows that each object of $\mathcal G$ is $\kappa$-compact.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9, opening; direct use of the accessibility and compactness definitions

proof.text: Let $\mathcal D\subseteq\mathcal C$ be the full subcategory on objects equivalent to apices of existing colimits of coherent diagrams $K\to\mathcal G$, where $K$ has fewer than $\kappa$ nondegenerate simplices. Only existing colimits are included. Apply the bounded-colimit clause of [lem-coef-locally-small-infinity-size-calculus] to the locally small $\mathcal C$, the essentially small $\mathcal G$ and the regular cardinal $\kappa$: it says precisely that $\mathcal D$ is essentially small. Each of these existing colimits has a $\kappa$-small shape and $\kappa$-compact vertex values by step 1. Since $\mathcal C$ admits small $\kappa$-filtered colimits, [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits] shows that every object of $\mathcal D$ is $\kappa$-compact. Equivalence of colimit apices does not change this property, since the induced mapping-space functors are equivalent.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9, bounded family of partial colimits and Corollary 5.3.4.15; using a chosen generating subcategory and all existing bounded colimits

proof.text: Fix $x\in\mathcal C$ and a small $\lambda$-filtered diagram $p:I\to\mathcal G$ with a colimiting cocone of apex $x$, supplied by step 1. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-kappa-poset] with its cardinal equal to $\lambda$ to obtain a small poset $A$ in which every subset of size less than $\lambda$ has an upper bound, and $u:N(A)\to I$. To justify restriction into the present $\mathcal C$, use the stated reindexing conclusion first with the infinity category $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ of small spaces. It admits all small colimits by [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe]. Consequently for every $H:I\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ the canonical comparison $\operatorname{colim}_{N(A)}Hu\to\operatorname{colim}_I H$ is an equivalence. This is condition (2) of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test], so condition (1) holds: restriction along $u$ preserves any existing colimiting cocone in every containing quasicategory. In particular $q=pu:N(A)\to\mathcal G$ has the restricted colimiting cocone of apex $x$. Both $I$ and $N(A)$ are small, as required by this test.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9, poset reindexing by Proposition 5.3.1.18; Proposition 4.1.1.8, with the space test made explicit (Kerodon Proposition 7.4.3.11)

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-sharp-filtered-poset-subsets] with $\alpha=\lambda$, $\beta=\kappa$ and the poset $A$. Its cardinal inequality is exactly the one in the hypothesis of the item. Obtain the small poset $\mathscr B$ of subsets $B\subseteq A$ of cardinality less than $\kappa$ which are $\lambda$-filtered in their inherited order. It covers $A$, is nonempty, and every family of fewer than $\kappa$ of its members has an upper bound. For a poset $P$ in which subsets of size less than a regular cardinal $\eta$ have upper bounds, its nerve is $\eta$-filtered directly: a map from an $\eta$-small simplicial set has fewer than $\eta$ image vertices; choose their upper bound $t$, and append $t$ to each image chain to obtain a compatible cocone. The empty test uses nonemptiness. Hence $N(B)$ is $\lambda$-filtered for each $B$, and $N(\mathscr B)$ is $\kappa$-filtered.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9, application of Lemma 5.4.2.8; Example 5.3.1.8 expanded as the append-an-upper-bound argument

proof.text: Each $N(B)$ is $\kappa$-small. Indeed $\kappa>\lambda\geq\aleph_0$, so $\kappa$ is uncountable. A nondegenerate $n$-simplex of $N(B)$ is a strictly increasing chain of $n+1$ elements of $B$, giving at most $|B|^{n+1}$ choices. Since $|B|<\kappa$ and $n+1<\lambda$, the cardinal inequality in the hypothesis gives $|B|^{n+1}<\kappa$ in every degree. There are countably many degrees; regularity and uncountability of $\kappa$ make their union have cardinality less than $\kappa$. Also $N(A)=\bigcup_{B\in\mathscr B}N(B)$: a simplex has finitely many vertices, and the containment assertion of step 4 puts that finite subset of $A$ in a single $B$. For each $B$, the restricted diagram $q|_{N(B)}$ has a colimiting cocone with apex $c_B$, because $N(B)$ is small and $\lambda$-filtered and $\mathcal C$ admits those colimits. Its shape is $\kappa$-small and its values belong to $\mathcal G$, so $c_B\in\mathcal D$ by the definition in step 2.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9, the bounded partial colimits; explicit nerve-size estimate and verification of their existence

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-directed-union-local-colimits] to $K=N(A)$, the small nonempty directed poset $\mathscr B$, the increasing simplicial subsets $N(B)$ covering $K$, the diagram $q$, and the chosen local colimit cocones with apices $c_B$. All its hypotheses were verified in steps 3-5; it assumes only these local colimits. It supplies a coherent assembly $c:N(\mathscr B)\to\mathcal C$ with vertices $c_B$ and identifies cocones on $c$ with compatible cocones on $q$, preserving the property of being colimiting. The colimiting cocone on $q$ with apex $x$ from step 3 therefore gives a colimiting cocone on $c$ with the same apex. Every vertex of $c$ lies in the full subcategory $\mathcal D$, so every simplex of $c$ lies in it as well; thus this is a small $\kappa$-filtered diagram in $\mathcal D$ presenting $x$.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9, final assembly using Propositions 4.2.3.4 and 4.2.3.8, Remark 4.2.3.9 and Corollary 4.2.3.10

proof.text: The category $\mathcal C$ is locally small and admits small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by step 1. The full subcategory $\mathcal D$ is essentially small and consists of $\kappa$-compact objects by step 2, and step 6 presents every object of $\mathcal C$ as a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit in $\mathcal D$. These are exactly the three clauses of $\kappa$-accessibility in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Therefore $\mathcal C$ is $\kappa$-accessible.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9, conclusion by the accessibility criterion of Proposition 5.4.2.2(3)

proof_origin.place: Expanded proof following HTT Proposition 5.4.2.9, printed p. 426 (PDF page 444), with existing DAG tools for size, compactness, cofinality and directed-union assembly. Online source is not archived in literature/.

lean.statement: theorem isKappaAccessible_of_sharp (C : SSet.{max (u + 1) v}) [SSet.Quasicategory C] (lam κ : Cardinal.{u}) (hlam : lam.IsRegular) (hκ : κ.IsRegular) (hlt : lam < κ) (hsharp : ∀ (μ ν : Cardinal.{u}), μ < κ → ν < lam → μ ^ ν < κ) (hC : IsKappaAccessible C lam) : IsKappaAccessible C κ
